title: Fail-safe: hold Dedicated staged rollouts when gate evaluator is degraded
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Context: Dedicated staged rollouts rely on the gate evaluator service to periodically compute gate outcomes (latency/error/queue depth/etc) and advance stages when gates pass. In dogfooding we saw cases where evaluator lag / missing windows caused rollouts to continue advancing based on stale state (or worse: keep advancing because no new failing signal was produced).

This PR makes evaluator health a first-class safety signal and changes stage advancement to fail closed.

Behavior change (fail-safe): If the evaluator is degraded, we force any rollout with auto-advance enabled into HOLD (reason=EVALUATOR_DEGRADED) and prevent automatic stage advancement until health recovers and a human explicitly resumes (Approve/Resume). Manual abort/rollback remains available.

What counts as degraded (v1): (1) evaluator heartbeat missing for > 2x tick interval for the rollout’s pool OR (2) evaluator is reporting evaluation backlog over threshold OR (3) metrics freshness check fails (no new datapoints beyond allowed staleness). All of these are evaluated per pool with guardrails to avoid flapping.

Implementation details: Added EvaluatorHealth to control-plane (stored per pool_id) and updated rollout state machine to require healthy evaluator for transitions RUNNING->ADVANCE_STAGE. Added HOLD reason codes and audit event emission for auto-hold. Routing/policy continues to respect last committed stage weights when a rollout is held (no traffic shift occurs during hold).

Observability: Added counters/gauges for evaluator health transitions, auto-holds, and blocked advancements. Added log fields rollout_plan_id, pool_id, stage_id, health_reason.

Tests: Unit tests for state transitions (healthy->advance allowed; degraded->auto-hold; recover->requires manual resume). Integration test updated to simulate evaluator lag and verify no stage advancement. Added a regression test to ensure evaluator degradation does not impact unrelated pools.

Risk/rollout: Feature-gated behind dedicatedStagedRolloutsFailsafeHold (default ON in staging, OFF in prod until SRE sign-off).
commits: control-plane: persist evaluator health per pool and expose via internal API
rollouts: add HOLD reason codes + block auto-advance when evaluator unhealthy
audit: emit rollout.auto_hold event when fail-safe triggers
telemetry: add evaluator health metrics + blocked advancement counters
tests: add evaluator-lag simulation and state machine coverage
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Love the direction. Two questions: (1) Where do we store the last-seen evaluator tick and do we handle clock skew? (2) Can we avoid auto-hold loops if the evaluator flaps every other tick?

Jordan Lee (author): (1) Storing server-side on control plane write path; evaluator includes observed window_end, but we compute staleness using control-plane receive time to avoid skew. (2) Added a 2-tick debounce + minimum hold duration (30s) before allowing resume, to avoid flapping causing rapid transitions.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure this is fail-closed for ANY auto-advance path, including the “approval arrives concurrently w/ tick” edge case. Also, can we add an alertable metric for rollouts blocked by evaluator health?

Jordan Lee (author): Updated transition guard to run in the single transition function used by both evaluator tick and approval handler. Added metric rollouts_stage_advancement_blocked_total{reason=evaluator_degraded} and a gauge rollouts_held_due_to_evaluator_health.
Logan Wright (review): Metrics freshness check: what’s the allowed staleness and is it configurable per tenant/pool? We’ve seen long ingestion delays during backfills.

Jordan Lee (author): Default staleness is 2m and configurable via pool config (control-plane). We also only apply freshness failures to auto-advance; manual approval can still proceed if operator decides it’s safe.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Any RBAC impact? Does auto-hold emit audit with actor=system and correct tenant/pool scoping?
Jordan Lee (author): No new permissions. Audit event uses actor_type=SYSTEM and includes tenant_id + pool_id + plan_version. Added test coverage for scoping and redaction of internal-only fields.

Chloe Martin (review): Console backend uses status summary; please ensure HOLD reason propagates so UI can show ‘Held (Evaluator degraded)’ and a clear CTA. Also, avoid breaking the existing status enum parsing.
Jordan Lee (author): Kept enum backward compatible; added new hold_reason field (string) and left status values unchanged. Console backend now maps it into the status payload.
Sean Gallagher (review): One more request: feature flag default should be ON in staging only. Prod default OFF until we validate alerting and runbook updates.
Jordan Lee (author): Done. Flag defaults updated (staging=on, prod=off).
Ethan Park (approve): Approved after debounce + unified guard changes. Ship it behind the flag.
Sean Gallagher (approve): Approved with the prod-default-off condition. Please link the oncall runbook in the dashboard doc.
Jordan Lee (author): Added link to runbook placeholder (will be updated in ENG-5133).
